<proposed_plan>
# Boardroom shared workspace and live agent activity rail

Opening any of the four workspace tabs should fold the orbital table fully to the left and give the center to the artist’s current task. A slim **live agent activity rail** on the right should tell the artist three things at a glance: **who’s working, what they’re doing, and whether they need attention**. The artist can operate the center directly or give the Conductor a mission and watch specialists work in that same space.

## 1. Give the work the room

- Replace the fixed three-column split with a flexible center, a **Show table** control at the left edge, and a 56-pixel agent rail on the right. Today the table and discussion reserve 60% of the width before the right rail opens. Opening discussion or agent details should slide out a drawer over the canvas. Closing it restores focus and preserves the chat draft, selected asset, studio draft, and browser page. [Current Boardroom layout](</Volumes/X SSD 2025/Users/narrowchannel/Desktop/indii-music-founder/packages/renderer/src/modules/boardroom/BoardroomModule.tsx:267>)
- Put the Conductor first in the rail, followed by seated specialists and an **Add agent** button. Selecting an avatar opens its assignment, latest action, and seating controls. Keep selecting, seating, soloing, and granting control distinct so inspecting an agent never interrupts the mission.
- Give motion a specific meaning. A working agent gets a softly moving ring, a real handoff briefly highlights the receiving specialist, and an approval request gets a persistent attention badge. Idle agents stay still. Pair every state with an icon and accessible label. Reduced-motion mode uses static indicators. On phones, use a compact team button that opens the same information in a sheet.

## 2. Let the artist and agents operate the same surface

| Workspace tab | What should work |
|---|---|
| **Live Browser** | In ordinary Chrome, open an isolated hosted browser in the center, including for portals that block iframe embedding. Support pointer, keyboard, scrolling, navigation history, reload, and reconnect. Reader and Pin to Swarm use the page actually visible in that session. Keep external open available when a provider requires it, and identify when control has moved outside the Boardroom. |
| **Studio Preview** | Keep the real Studio modules interactive. Give specialists typed actions for the same module controls the artist uses. For example, Creative can open Image Studio, set the prompt and aspect ratio, and leave the draft visible for the artist to edit or generate. Size toolbars and forms to the pane, fix the overlapping navigation shown in the screenshot, and retain drafts across tab changes. |
| **Asset Workbench** | Open the exact media item, artifact, split sheet, or canvas panel named by the artist or returned by an agent. Today only media targets are honored. Connect web artifacts to authenticated project storage, distinguish loading and failure from an empty project, and offer **Open Studio** when the artist has no media yet. Pin, export, and studio handoff must act on the selected item. |
| **Agent Live Feed** | Connect the feed to actual Boardroom mission steps, tool results, handoffs, approvals, and failures. Use the same events for the right rail. Make **Stop mission** revoke control and cancel queued work on web and desktop. Show the acknowledged outcome, including any external action already in flight. Today the web button can report a stop without issuing one. |

## 3. Make delegation and takeover reliable

- Build the hosted browser on the streaming, input, and handoff mechanisms already used by the rights-filing viewport. Give Boardroom its own session policy. Keep the existing filing restrictions and the native Electron browser, with desktop controls scoped to its Boardroom view. [Existing hosted viewport](</Volumes/X SSD 2025/Users/narrowchannel/Desktop/indii-music-founder/packages/renderer/src/modules/registration/components/HostedRightsViewport.tsx>) · [Existing browser worker](</Volumes/X SSD 2025/Users/narrowchannel/Desktop/indii-music-founder/packages/rights-browser-worker/src/index.ts>)
- Route Conductor assignments through one typed workspace action interface. Each action identifies the mission, assigned specialist, target, and requested operation, and returns a result the UI can verify. Reuse the existing Boardroom tab-opening actions and module services. A specialist opening Studio should reveal it **inside the Boardroom**.
- Let specialists research public HTTPS destinations relevant to the mission, navigate, read, and pin evidence. Route account-changing actions through verified integrations and their existing approvals. Sign-in and MFA belong to the artist, with agent observation suspended during credential entry.
- Give one participant control of the visible surface at a time. Show **You have control** or the specialist’s name beside **Take control**. Taking over immediately invalidates queued agent input. The artist explicitly hands control back. Bind commands to the current session, page revision, and control grant so a delayed click cannot land on a different page. Reconnect must recover the actual page and owner before enabling input.

## 4. Prove it with one complete mission

Use an artist’s genuine account in ordinary Chrome. Ask the Conductor to have one specialist research a supplied page and pin a reference, then have Creative use that reference to prepare artwork. Take over mid-draft, edit the prompt, return control, and open the resulting asset in Workbench. The artist should be able to follow the entire sequence from the rail, inspect the matching receipts in Live Feed, and stay inside the Boardroom throughout.

Also verify all four tabs with mouse and keyboard, narrow layouts, reduced motion, native Electron overlays, a frame-blocking portal, stale input after takeover, disconnect and reconnect, and Stop during queued work. Test each advertised portal through its official entry point and record any provider or sign-in limitation individually. Deliver through Entire on `main` and check CI for the pushed SHA.

The current findings come from the supplied screenshots and source inspection. Live portal behavior and the proposed shared-control journey still need genuine-account verification.
</proposed_plan>
